title: SB2055 (2020 Regular): Firearms restraining order; create the Red Flag Law.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2020/html/SB/2001-2099/SB2055IN.htm)
provenance.note: Introduced text as filed; no passage vote. Quoted parts are the core of Section 1; its other subsections cover service, six-month orders, renewal, hearings and fee waivers. Section 3 only brings forward 25-7-9 (chancery fees). The title also promises licence revocation on an order; the text read has the three-year bar in Section 2 but no revocation wording was found.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new section, subsection (2)): "Extreme risk protection order" means an order issued by the court, prohibiting and enjoining a named person from purchasing, possessing or receiving, or having in the person's custody or control, any firearms. The affiant must be either a family member of the respondent or a law enforcement officer. If the chancellor finds probable cause to believe that the respondent poses an immediate and present danger of causing personal injury to himself, herself, or another by purchasing, possessing or receiving, or having in his or her custody or control, a firearm, the chancellor shall issue an emergency order. (ii) If the court issues an emergency extreme risk protection order, upon a finding of probable cause that the respondent possesses firearms, it shall issue a search warrant directing a law enforcement agency to seize the respondent's firearms. A respondent who knowingly violates an extreme risk protection order is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by a fine not to exceed One Thousand Dollars ($1,000.00) and confinement in the county jail not to exceed one (1) year.
Section 2 (Miss. Code § 45-9-101): (m) Has not been subject to an extreme risk protection order under Section 1 of this act for at least three (3) years.
